Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our mutual action plan, we want to lock the environment items that will unblock the evaluation + close in the next two weeks. I pulled together the minimal ops sprint we discussed — attached as "RDW_ClearBridge_MAP_v1.xlsx" — and a short list of the infra artifacts your team will need to confirm so we can provision the evaluation environment.

High level asks (target: environment ready by Fri, Aug 20):
- Org setup: Please confirm an initial org admin account (email) we can invite to the Redwood console for the trial.
- API keys: We will generate evaluation API keys and rotate them after the trial; need a service account / owner to link them to.
- IP allowlist: Add the attached ip-allowlist.csv ranges to your perimeter for test traffic (port 443).
- VPC peering: If you want private connectivity, please sign the attached vpc_peering_template.txt and provide the VPC CIDR + AWS account ID.

If procurement needs any paperwork before signing, loop them in — we can ship a one-page SOW and a short DocuSign to keep timelines tight.

Next steps I propose:
1) Priya confirms admin email + whether you want public (IP allowlist) or private (VPC peering) connectivity by EOD Thu, Aug 13.
2) Karthik will run a short architecture sync (30m) to validate peering/egress requirements — available Fri morning.
3) Marissa to provision evaluation keys and send test curl examples once network is OK.

Attaching: RDW_ClearBridge_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP sprint), vpc_peering_template.txt, ip-allowlist.csv

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out quickly.

Hi Priya —

Quick answers to the technical bits:

- Token TTL: For evaluation keys we can set a TTL of 14 days by default. Keys can be created with scoped permissions (e.g., embeddings only, generate only). For your eval, we usually recommend two keys: one scoped to embeddings + rerank (for model comparisons) and one for generation calls.
- SSO: Not required for the trial. Standard email invites will work and are the quickest way to get your engineers in the console. We can reconfigure to SSO later as part of production onboarding.

Networking notes for your team when they open the firewall ticket:
- IP ranges: See ip-allowlist.csv. Add outbound to 34.210.12.0/24 and 52.23.98.0/24 (HTTPS) for test traffic; we will fall back to TLS over standard ports.
- VPC peering: If you choose peering later, we'll need your VPC ID, account ID, and preferred AZs. Our template includes the route table changes to expect.

I can do a 30-minute sync tomorrow (Fri Aug 14) at 9:00am PT to walk through the peering checklist and run a test curl once the IPs are allowed. If that works for you I’ll send a calendar invite.

—
